newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's Van Miert to restate EBU sports TV rights.
newsitem.headline: EU's Van Miert to restate EBU sports TV rights.

text.p: European Union Competition Commissioner Karel van Miert said on Thursday the Commission was expected to re-adopt a decision allowing the European Broadcasting Union (EBU) to negotiate exclusive sports television broadcasting rights, but with a few changes.

In July, the European Court of Justice annulled a European Commission decision of June 1993 which granted the EBU an exemption from competition restrictions when acquiring exclusive rights to sports events.
EBU, which groups 67 European public radio and television organisations, said at the time the court ruling meant that the Commission would have to take a new decision.

"We are currently carrying out an in-depth assessment of the Court's decision but we think that as to the substance there is no reason to change our decision," Van Miert told the European Parliament's economic and monetary committee.
"We will have to modify a few things," Van Miert said, referring to the European Court's objections regarding the presence among current EBU shareholders of French pay-TV channel Canal Plus.

Van Miert said that he was increasingly worried about the acquisition by some large media groups of exclusive broadcasting rights. He said that in this context public broadcasters had no alternative but to get together.
